For the Petitioner : Mr. Manoj Tandon, Advocate  Ms. Neha Bhardwaj, Advocate  Mr. Adamya Kerketta, Advocate For the Lokayukta: : Mr. Rajesh Kumar, Advocate For the A.C.B. : Mr. Rakesh Ranjan, A.C. to G.A.-I For the Resp. Sinha, Advocate 09/Dated: 19/09/2023 Heard Mr. Manoj Tandon, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Rajesh Kumar, learned counsel for the Lokayukta, Mr. Rakesh Ranjan, learned counsel for the ACB and Mr. P.C. Sinha, learned counsel for the respondent no. 4.
2.

This petition has been filed for quashing the decision contained in letter dated 31.10.2017 contained in Annexure-3 issued by the respondent no. 3 to investigate the private property of the petitioner and others and report was called for by the Lokayukta before 12.12.2017 3.
Mr. Manoj Tandon, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that a complaint was filed by the respondent no. 4 before the Hon'ble Lokayukta, Jharkhand swearing an affidavit on 09.09.2013.

He refers to para 11 and 12 of the complaint filed by the respondent no. 4 wherein it is alleged inter alia that this petitioner went to jail in the year, 1995 and there is allegation of misappropriation of public Kamala Singh vs Office Of Hon'Ble Lokayukta on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121607154/
1 fund by the petitioner while he was posted as Block Education Extension Officer in Nagar Untari,
Garhwa and misappropriation of amount with regard to bonus amount by the peon of the petitioner namely, Satyanaryan Ram thrice in a year and the petitioner was posted as lecturer from 2001-2005 in Training College, Latehar and the petitioner was also incharge of Block Education Extension Officer, Chandwa and Balumath and at that point of time he opened 250 Abhiyan Vidayalaya without children and norms in Chandwa and Balumath and therefore complaint was made.
4.

sentences.text: Mr. Tandon, further submits that complaint was made on 09.09.2013 wherein allegations are for the period of 1995-2005.
He submits that in view of sub-section 4 (a) and (b) of Section 8 of the Jharkhand Lokayukta Act, 2001 the said investigation is barred by time.
He refers to Section 10 of said Act and submits that no opportunity was provided to the petitioner and in view of that the said notice is bad in law.

He further submits that the allegation made hereinabove against the petitioner has already been exonerated by the competent criminal Court by judgment dated 29.02.2016 in G.R.
No. 414 of 1995.
On these grounds, he submits that this petition may be allowed.

5. On the other hand, Mr. Rajesh Kumar, learned counsel for the Lokayukta submits that this is a premature petition filed by the petitioner and only preliminary enquiry has been called upon with regard to disproportionate assets of the petitioner.
He submits that once the Lokayukta will come to the conclusion to proceed further after preliminary enquiry Section 10 of the said Act will come into play.
He further submits that in view of sub-section 3 of Section 10 of Act the Lokayukta can proceed as he considers appropriate in the circumstances of the case.
He further submits that this aspect of the matter has already been set at rest by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of "Rang Nath Mishra V. State of U.P" (2015) 8 SCC 117.

entities.text: Rang Nath Mishra V. State of U.P" (2015) 8 SCC 117
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He refers to para 19, 20 and 21 of the said judgment which are quoted here-in-below:-
"19.
Though the first complaint (undated) submitted by Respondent 4 was not addressed to the Lokayukta, U.P., the reminder dated 27-8-2010 was addressed, inter alia, to the Lokayukta, U.P.
If that is so, there is no reason why the same cannot be understood to be a complaint to the Lokayukta, U.P. for further action on the basis thereof.

If reception/acceptance of a subsequent affidavit of the complainant in support of a complaint filed earlier is contemplated by Rule 5 of the Rules, we do not see why any fault can be found in the action of the Lokayukta, U.P. in accepting the affidavit dated 22-12- 2010 submitted by the complainant.

Though the notice dated 18-10- 2010 for preliminary enquiry was issued at an earlier stage, it is by the communication dated 14-2-2011 (after receipt of the affidavit dated 22-12-2010) that the appellant was informed that the complaint of Respondent 4 has been accepted for investigation under Section 10(1)(a) of the Act.

If, in the light of the aforesaid facts,
the Lokayukta, U.P. had decided to proceed further in the matter and had issued communications to the appellant asking for his reply and documents in defence which were adequately responded to by the appellant on several dates, as noticed earlier, we do not see how the appellant can be understood to be justified in raising the issue of defect of procedure before the High Court and before this Court.
The capitulation of the relevant dates and events leave no room for doubt that all requirements under the Act have been complied with in the instant case.

sentences.text:
While it is correct that the Report of the Lokayukta was submitted without affording any opportunity of personal hearing to the appellant and the request for time for submission of the documents made by the appellant on 29-9-2011 was refused by the Lokayukta, the said facts cannot constitute a good and sufficient basis for this Court to find fault with the conduct of the proceedings by the Lokayukta, U.P.
in view of the provisions of Section 10(3) of the Act which, as already noticed, leaves to the Lokayukta the discretion to adopt such procedure as may be considered appropriate in the given facts of the case.
No prejudice also has been caused to the appellant who had taken part in the proceedings at every stage.

The refusal to grant further time to the appellant, an issue over which some grievance has been raised, is a matter of discretion vested in the Lokayukta and any decision thereon either way cannot be a legitimate basis for interference.
21. Before parting, the issue with regard to the jurisdiction of the Lokayukta to proceed in the instant matter in view of the provisions of the Third Schedule to the Act must be answered.

What the Third Schedule to the Act contemplates is that the Lokayukta in the course of an investigation under the Act will not investigate a crime or determine the question as to whether the matter "shall go to, or shall continue to be prosecuted in a court or not".
In the present case, the recommendations of the Lokayukta were merely for an investigation as to whether a case for prosecution of the appellant is made out or not.
Accordingly, the matter was investigated and presently is under trial in a court of competent jurisdiction.

All the said subsequent facts as noted in detail at the very outset make it clear that even if the contentions of the appellant with regard to the Third Schedule to the Act are to be accepted (we make it clear that we do not accept the same), the question that would arise has become wholly academic."
6. He further submits that so far exoneration in criminal proceeding is concerned that is another aspect of the matter that was only under I.P.C. sections i.e 409, 420 and 467 of the I.P.C.
He submits that in the present case the Prevention of Corruption Act is involved.
He submits that notice was with regard to disproportionate assets of the petitioner.
On these grounds he submits that at this stage, this petition may not be entertained as the petition is premature.

7. Mr. P.C. Sinha, learned counsel for the respondent no. 4 submits that in the complaint allegation is made about the irregularities made by this petitioner while he was posted as a Block Education Extension Officer of that area.
He submits that the impugned notice that is for the subject matter and only disproportionate assets of the petitioner has been sought to be enquired by the Lokayukta.
He submits that there are other persons involved and in the criminal case and only the petitioner has been exonerated.
On these grounds, he submits that this petition is fit to be dismissed.

8. In view of above submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, the Court has gone through the materials on record and finds that in the complaint the allegations are made against the petitioner that when the petitioner was posted as Block Education Extension Officer, Nagar Untari,
Garhwa at that point of time the peon of this petitioner namely Satyanaryan Ram withdrew the Kamala Singh vs Office Of Hon'Ble Lokayukta on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121607154/
3 amount of bonus thrice in a year and the petitioner was posted at Lecturer from 2001-2002 in Training College, Latehar and was also incharge of Block Education Extension Officer, Chandwa and Balumath and at that point of time he opened 250 Abhiyan Vidayalaya without children and norms in Chandwa and Balumath, Latehar.

sentences.text: By the impugned order dated 31.10.2017 the report was sought for with regard to the disproportionate assets of the petitioner on or before 12.12.2017.

Thus, it appears that Lokayukta has not taken any final decision with regard to the disproportionate assets of the petitioner and only he has sought report with regard to disproportionate assets of the petitioner.
In this impugned order the period is not prescribed so far the allegation made for the period 1995-2005 is concerned, in the complaint the allegations are otherwise.
Further the Court finds that this Annexure-3 was not communicated to the petitioner and neither obtained under R.T.I. Act.
The question remains how the petitioner has come to the knowledge about this Annexure-3 which creates serious doubt.
Sub-section 4 (a) and 4 (b) of Section 8 of the Act relates to the matters not subject to investigation.

Section 8 of the Jharkhand Lokayukta Act, 2001 is quoted here- in-under:-
" 8.

Matters not subject to investigation (1) Except as hereinafter provided the Lokayukta shall not conduct any investigation under this Act in the case of complaint involving a grievance in respect of any action- (a) If such action relate to any matter specified in the Third Schedule; or (b) If the complaint has or had any remedy by way of proceedings before any Tribunal or Court of law: Provided that the Lokayukta may conduct an investigation notwithstanding that the complainant had or has such a remedy if he is satisfied that such person could not or cannot for sufficient cause have recourse to such remedy.

(5) In the case of any complaint Kamala Singh vs Office Of Hon'Ble Lokayukta on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121607154/
4 involving a grievance

sentences.text: nothing in this Act shall be construed as empowering the Lokayukta to question any administrative action involving the exercise of a discretion, except where he is satisfied that the elements involved in the exercise of the discretion are absent to such an extent that the discretion cannot be regarded as having been properly exercised.

9. In Section 10 of the Jharkhand Lokayukta Act, 2001 procedure is prescribed therein which stipulates as under:-
"10. Procedure in respect of investigation.(1)

(4-A) The Lokayukta shall not proceed with any investigation under this Act where the Supreme Court or the High Court issues any direction, order or writ under Article 32 of Article 226 of the Constitution of India in respect of the matter mentioned in the complaint under investigation.

(5) In any case whether the Lokayukta decides not to entertain a complaint or is discontinue any investigation in respect of a complaint, he Kamala Singh vs Office Of Hon'Ble Lokayukta on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121607154/
5 shall record his reasons therefor and communicate the same to the complainant and the public servant concerned.

entities.text: Kamala Singh vs Office Of Hon'Ble Lokayukta
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(6) The conduct of an investigation under this Act in respect of any action shall not affect such action, or any power or duty of any public servant to take further action with respect to any matter subject to the investigation."
10. Looking into Sub-section 3 of the Section 10 of Jharkhand Lokayukta Act, 2001, it appears that the Lokayukta has been provided discretion to proceed as he considers appropriate in the circumstances of the case and this section has already been considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and answer is already there in para 19, 20 and 21 in Rang Nath Mishra (supra) relied by Mr.
Rajesh Kumar, learned counsel for the Lokayukta.

11. The Court finds that so far acquittal of the petitioner in G.R. No. 414 of 1995 is concerned that was with respect to allegations under sections 409, 420, 467 of the I.P.C. and only on one technicality the petitioner was acquitted as not even a single witness was adduced by the prosecution in the entire trial.
It is well settled that even in a criminal case on the technicality acquittal is there, the benefit of that cannot be extended with regard to other proceeding.
12. It appears that the petitioner was not noticed as yet, stage has not come and once final decision is taken by the Lokayukta without hearing the petitioner the matter may would have otherwise.
The point of limitation has been considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in para 20 of the aforesaid judgment relied by the learned counsel for the Lokayukta.
13. Further considering that the corruption has spread its tentacle in almost all the key areas of the State and it is an impediment to the growth and development of State as well as of the country.
There has to be stern action by all the concerns particularly the government and there should be public awareness against the corruption.
14. In view of above facts, reasons and analysis there is no illegality in the impugned order.
No relief can be extended to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this petition is dismissed.
Interim order is vacated.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Satyarthi/
